memoryText: Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and do not lean on your own understanding. In all your ways acknowledge him, and he will make straight your paths.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read Proverbs 3:5-6 once more, several times, and then say it from memory. Read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
You memorized this verse in the last unit. Today, return to it with the opening of the divided kingdom in mind.

Rehoboam leaned on his own understanding. He took the counsel of his young friends and refused the advice of the elders. The result was a torn nation. Jeroboam leaned on his own understanding too. He feared losing his people and invented a new religion. The result was a sin that haunted a kingdom for two hundred years. Both are living illustrations of what happens when we do not trust the LORD with all our heart.

The verse does not say that thinking is bad. It says that our own understanding is not the final guide. We are limited. We cannot see the future. We cannot see the heart of another. We cannot be sure of our own motives. When we rest our whole weight on what seems wise to us, we are in danger.

“In all your ways acknowledge him.” Rehoboam did not consult God. He did not ask. Jeroboam did not ask either. He worked out a plan that made sense politically. But acknowledging the LORD means bringing him into the decision, before we act. It means asking, “What has God said?”

“And he will make straight your paths.” Note that this is a promise for those who trust. God will direct the paths. This is a comfort for anyone who has made a mess of things. It is not too late to begin trusting.

Hold this verse as the unit moves into a darker period. In a time of idolatry and violence, the way to stay faithful is not to rely on our own cleverness but on the LORD.
weekInReview: This week the united kingdom of David and Solomon came apart. You read of Rehoboam’s proud answer and Jeroboam’s golden calves, and the sin of Jeroboam that became the standard of evil for the northern kings. You saw how God kept a lamp for David’s sake in Jerusalem, even as Judah’s kings failed. You followed the quick succession of northern kings, with their coups, until Ahab and Jezebel brought Baal worship into the heart of Israel. The week taught that a proud word can tear a nation, that convenient religion is idolatry, and that God keeps his promises to David even when his people do not keep theirs.
reflectionQuestions: Rehoboam refused the counsel of the elders. Who are the wise people in your life, and are you listening to them?
God kept a lamp burning for David’s sake even when Judah’s kings failed. How does Christ, the true Son of David, give you confidence that God keeps his promises?
Jeroboam designed a religion that was convenient. Where are you tempted to adjust your faith to fit your comfort?
prayerPrompts: Tell God you trust him with all your heart, and name one thing you lean on yourself for.
Thank him for keeping his promises to David and for Christ the true king.
